quest.title: The Strange Tale of Suikou's Tipsy Tincture
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x40, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x3

chapter.num: True Tales of the Violet Garden: Act I
chapter.title: The Strange Tale of Suikou's Tipsy Tincture

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What is it, Venti? A piece of paper?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Indeed. When I awakened to find myself in the warehouse this morning, I discovered this paper in the cargo crate where I was sleeping.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: I didn't think much of it then, I thought it was merely a scrap piece of paper that had fallen into the cargo. After a quick glance, I stuffed it into a place nearby.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: But on second thought, I think it's worth having you take a look at what's written on it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let me see... "Suikou Chapter"? Wait a minute, isn't Suikou the name of one of The Five Kasen?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: The story told in this poem roughly boils down to Suikou getting tipsy and letting some poems that were meant for the Shogun get stolen.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Huh, this story sounds familiar to my ear, where have I heard it...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Seriously!? It's literally the same story you just experienced yesterday!

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Ahahaha. Indeed, it is. Interesting, isn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It almost seems related to the stolen novels.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Yes, I concur. The person who left this paper could quite possibly be the criminal or even a witness to the theft.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: But why leave the paper here in such a fashion? And if the one who left it here was a witness, why didn't they attempt to stop the burglary?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: All right, let's not get ahead of ourselves.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Meeting together in Inazuma like this is a most rare occasion. Since we've been busy from the start of the day, let us find an inn with good drink to keep our thirst at bay!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! You just sobered up and you're already thinking about more drinks?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And let's not forget that Albedo still has a portrait to complete. We don't have time to be slacking off!

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: No, it's fine. Let's all go for a drink together. It'll be my treat.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait a minute, what about your portrait?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: As I mentioned before, I'm the kind of artist who can work quickly once I'm inspired. And now, it seems I've found my source of inspiration.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: If I use a model as reference for the piece, we must pay him back with the appropriate recompense.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Haha, in that case, we'll need to order more dishes!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hello! You must be here to take part in the Irodori Festival? We're the festival guides and will show you around.

dialogues.speaker: Lyra
dialogues.text: Yes, that's right. We are bards from Mondstadt.

dialogues.speaker: Lyra
dialogues.text: Word has it that Inazuma has undergone many changes of late. We hope to find fresh inspiration here.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Uh, Paimon? What are you doing?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: These guests are all bards, aren't they? Well, where's Tone-Deaf Bard then?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Strange, he is pretty famous in Mondstadt... Do you think he didn't receive an invitation?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Even if he was invited, there's a chance he still wouldn't show up.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, why's that?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Well, you know. Venti's an...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh... Paimon sees what you're getting at. Even though Venti no longer rules over Mondstadt, he's still an archon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If he came rushing to Inazuma at the first mention of a festival, not only would it seem a little childish, it would also sorta be shameless of him, too.

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: #{F#Miss}{M#Mr.} Honorary Knight! Paimon!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's Klee! Were you also invited to the Irodori Festival?

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: No, Albedo's the one who received the invitation.

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: But because everyone in the Knights of Favonius has been really busy these days, Albedo arranged for someone here to issue me a Dependant Pass.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: #Greetings, {NICKNAME} and Paimon. After hearing that Inazuma was making preparations for the Irodori Festival, I predicted that I might run into you here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hah, Paimon knew it! Albedo's the one they've invited to paint The Five Kasen.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: It seems that you already know why I'm here. Just so you're aware, I'll be using my pen name in Inazuma, Calx.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: By the way, do you know where the International Trade Association is? I'll be meeting with the editorial director of the Yae Publishing House there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, the International Trade Association is where you'll be staying in Inazuma. We'll be heading there, too.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Great, let's get going then.

talks.objective: Go to the International Trade Association

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: This can't be happening! The moment we need to contact Onodera is when he's on special leave.

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: Kuroda and I will go back to Inazuma City for an emergency printing run. The demand for this book is so high though, even with the emergency prints it still might not be enough.

dialogues.speaker: Murata
dialogues.text: Despite everything, we're still lucky that we found out today. If this had happened a few days later, then we'd really be in boiling water.

dialogues.speaker: Murata
dialogues.text: *sigh* Hey, do you think that the suspicious guy they found in the warehouse has anything to do with this?

dialogues.speaker: Kuroda
dialogues.text: Well, the editorial director is on his way over there to investigate the situation as we speak.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, sorry to interrupt, but what's going on here?

dialogues.speaker: Murata
dialogues.text: Oh, hey Traveler. Don't worry, it's nothing. Just an internal issue, that's all. How can I help you?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I'm looking for the editorial director, Mr. Hirayama. Does anyone know where he is now?

dialogues.speaker: Murata
dialogues.text: Mr. Hirayama is currently at the warehouse down by the harbor...

dialogues.speaker: Kuroda
dialogues.text: Hold on a second, Murata.

dialogues.speaker: Kuroda
dialogues.text: Uh, excuse me, but you must be Calx, the one who was invited to paint The Five Kasen for the festival?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Yes, that's me.

dialogues.speaker: Kuroda
dialogues.text: My name is Kuroda. You must be inquiring about information regarding The Five Kasen.

dialogues.speaker: Kuroda
dialogues.text: I do apologize, but please make yourself comfortable at the International Trade Association, and I will let Mr. Hirayama know to send you the materials right away.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, no need! You guys look super busy, so we can go find him ourselves.

dialogues.speaker: Kuroda
dialogues.text: Ah well, a—about that...

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Excuse me, but is there something wrong with the latest volume of A Legend of Sword?

dialogues.speaker: Kuroda
dialogues.text: Huh! How did you know?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Since you were all aware that Mr. Hirayama needed to send me some supporting materials, that means the editorial director didn't forget about it. Instead, something urgent must've cropped up.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: To add to that, despite being aware that I am Calx, you are still unwilling to let me go to Mr. Hirayama directly.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: After considering these factors, the only reason you would try to stall me is if something happened to A Legend of Sword, which I did the illustrations for.

dialogues.speaker: Kuroda
dialogues.text: Well, uh... *sigh* I'm very sorry. The situation is just as you said, Calx. I suppose it doesn't hurt to tell you now...

dialogues.speaker: Kuroda
dialogues.text: Earlier today, someone spotted a suspicious outlander sneaking around inside the Irodori Festival warehouse down by the docks, so they promptly alerted the Tenryou Commission.

dialogues.speaker: Kuroda
dialogues.text: The Tenryou Commission was concerned about potential cargo theft, so they contacted everyone who was renting space in the warehouse. It was then that we realized that the latest copies of A Legend of Sword had suddenly gone missing!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What? The books are missing!?

dialogues.speaker: Kuroda
dialogues.text: Shh... Not so loud!

dialogues.speaker: Kuroda
dialogues.text: Not only is this book an eagerly anticipated release in the last phase of the Irodori Festival, but the author, Zhenyu, will be personally attending the release party as well.

dialogues.speaker: Murata
dialogues.text: Because of the dire situation, Mr. Hirayama immediately hurried to the warehouse to determine whether the theft was related to that suspicious outlander.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I see. It would be a great misfortune if A Legend of Sword would not be released on schedule, and quite the disappointment for Zhenyu as well.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: If Mr. Hirayama has gone to the warehouse at the docks, then I'll go down to see if I can be of any help.

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: Wow, it's so beautiful here. So many things I've never seen before!

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Slow down, Klee. Please, be careful not to bump into others.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: *sigh* Telling Klee so many stories about Inazuma during the trip was probably not the best idea.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: As a result, she could hardly sleep all the way here. It appears she's even more excited now that we've arrived.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Strange... It seems that the editorial director, Mr. Hirayama, isn't here yet. I'm certain he said that he'd be sure to arrive before me. This might be a problem.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What's wrong?

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Well, Mr. Hirayama was supposed to meet with me and give me some reference materials about The Five Kasen today. That way, I could better visualize the content for my paintings.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You mean you had no idea what you'd be painting before you arrived in Inazuma?

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: I only know of The Five Kasen by name. Because of the sheer age of the tale, very little has been passed down to this day, so Mr. Hirayama decided to help me collect some more information.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: I'm the type of painter who can complete a painting quickly as long as I'm inspired. So I agreed on only receiving the details today.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So when do the paintings have to be done by?

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: According to the festival plans, the portraits will be revealed one at a time throughout the various stages of the Irodori Festival. The first one depicting Suikou will need to be done before the festival's official opening ceremony, which is the day after tomorrow.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The day after tomorrow!? Then you're already running out of time!

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: There's no need to panic. When I was working on light novel illustrations, because the manuscripts are shipped by boat, things were always tight and finished at the last minute.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Just last month, to ensure the latest book of A Legend of Sword would be finished for the Irodori Festival, I had to complete the final chapter's illustrations the same day I received the manuscript.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: I heard that my illustrations were sent to print as soon as they arrived in Inazuma. I still don't know how well they turned out.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... Paimon isn't sure if she should feel sympathetic for your working conditions, or compliment you on your artistic genius.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Of course, I would still prefer to receive any possible reference materials in advance so that I can be better prepared.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Speaking of which, Miko did mention...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, right! The editors of the Yae Publishing House will all be around the Outlander Affairs Agency these next few days.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Who knows, maybe Mr. Hirayama's over there too. We'll take you over there to see if we can find him, Albedo!

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Alright, it's worth a try. Klee, you haven't slept for a while now. Please stay at our residence in the International Trade Association and get some rest. We will be back soon.

response.speaker: Klee
response.text: Okey-dokey. Don't worry, Albedo, I'll be on my best behavior!

choices.text: Nothing wrong with a little excitement.

talks.objective: Go to the Outlander Affairs Agency

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There goes Sara. Alright, let's go talk to Mr. Hirayama about Albedo's reference materials.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Mr. Hirayama, I'm Calx. We had originally arranged to meet today.

dialogues.speaker: Hirayama
dialogues.text: Ah, yes, so you are Calx! I'm very sorry that you've arrived in Inazuma only to find such a mess.

dialogues.speaker: Hirayama
dialogues.text: These are the materials regarding The Five Kasen. All the information that we could find is compiled here.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Let's see here... Yes, it's just as I had suspected. Monikers such as "Suikou" and "Aoi no Okina" aren't the real names of The Five Kasen.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: "Though there were once many stories regarding each of The Five Kasen, the validity of their contents can no longer be verified in present times." ...Alas, what a shame.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: But at the very least we know that most of the stories were written according to a similar style, so there is still something we may glean from this.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So is the info useful for your paintings, Albedo?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: To some extent, yes. However, I must admit that it is still lacking, and fails to fulfill the most crucial element... inspiration.

dialogues.speaker: Hirayama
dialogues.text: I am sorry that this information is not as exhaustive as you'd hoped. However, it is not possible to gather anything more at the moment.

dialogues.speaker: Hirayama
dialogues.text: Though, Lady Yae did say that there are many variations of the stories about The Five Kasen, and everyone has a different story in their heart.

dialogues.speaker: Hirayama
dialogues.text: So all you need to do is to follow through with what's in your own heart and create something that you yourself find interesting.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That does sound like something Miko would say.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Thank you, Mr. Hirayama. No need to worry, I'll find inspiration for the portraits.

dialogues.speaker: Hirayama
dialogues.text: Great. I'll leave it to you then, Calx. Oh, and there's one more thing I need to ask of everyone.

dialogues.speaker: Hirayama
dialogues.text: Tomorrow morning Mr. Zhenyu, the author of A Legend of Sword, will be arriving in Inazuma by boat. If you see him, please do not mention the stolen novels for the time being.

dialogues.speaker: Hirayama
dialogues.text: Whether the stolen books are eventually recovered or not, the Yae Publishing House will do its best to ensure that the novel's release is a success!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I get it now.

dialogues.speaker: Hirayama
dialogues.text: You have my gratitude. I'll be going, then.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, seems there's nothing more we can do here. Let's go.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Venti? What are you doing over there? You don't want us to leave you behind, do you?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Albedo, would you mind coming over here for a moment? There's something peculiar that I think you should see.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So the author of A Legend of Sword is Zhenyu, sounds familiar... Hey, isn't that Xingqiu's pen name?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Oh? Do you know him?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We've met on a couple of occasions.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Xingqiu would definitely be upset if he discovers that his books are missing... Let's accompany Albedo to the warehouse, too.

talks.objective: Go to the warehouse near the docks

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: In his hat?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: #Ah yes, I remember now. I knew you'd help me find it, {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Venti finds the Invitation Letter stuffed under his hat...

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Sara
dialogues.text: Hmm. This is indeed an Invitation Letter issued by the Yashiro Commission. Now that we've confirmed this guest's identity, I have no further questions.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Sara
dialogues.text: However, starting tonight, I would advise you to stay at the International Trade Association.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Sara
dialogues.text: Now, if you'll excuse me, I'll be leaving now.

talks.objective: Go and talk to Albedo at The Five Kasen Plaza

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, you really came through, Albedo. You were able to complete the first portrait before the opening ceremony.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Yes, it really is a sight to behold. Not only does it hearken to the traditional style of Inazuma, but it also makes use of modern aesthetics. My figure is particularly striking, even though I'm sound asleep in the portrait, I still appear as glorious as always.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, don't get too full of yourself, Tone-Deaf Bard! You were just a model, the person in the artwork isn't actually you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, Albedo, who will be your next portrait?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: The next one will be Aoi no Okina of The Five Kasen.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Albedo, might I suggest waiting a little before starting on the next one? Who knows, you might soon discover another story.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Another story?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I believe he's referring to the possibility of finding another paper with tales of The Five Kasen. According to the reference materials I was given, we've only found the first of a total of four chapters.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Do you think the mysterious person who left the first paper will strike again?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: It certainly is a possibility. Also, there are some points regarding the stories of The Five Kasen that have left me rather curious.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: For example, the reference materials make mention of five legendary figures, yet all the popular stories only consist of four parts.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: It appears that throughout all the stories, there is never a chapter dedicated to Kuronushi.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Yes, I'm also curious about these stories myself. But who knows, they may merely be akin to the old saying in Mondstadt: "Seeds of stories, brought by the wind and cultivated by time."

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: So, for now, we need but just wait patiently.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? It's you...! Why are you here!?

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Sara
dialogues.text: I'm here on behalf of the Tenryou Commission, of course. Is that surprising?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No, Sara, Paimon wasn't talking about you...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, Tone-Deaf Bard... The suspicious outlander in the warehouse wouldn't happen to be you, would it?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Ehe... Considering the evidence, it appears that the suspicious outlander is... indeed me.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Sara
dialogues.text: As I have told you, you are a suspect. Before your allegations of theft and illegal entry as a stowaway are cleared, you are to remain silent. Don't make me say it again.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Sara
dialogues.text: Traveler, Paimon, do you know this self-proclaimed bard from Mondstadt?

choices.text: Well, I can't say he's a complete stranger...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, listen Sara... Knowing him, it's safe to say that he wasn't behind the theft. But, what's this about being a stowaway?

response.speaker: Kujou Sara
response.text: Although he claims to be a special guest for the Irodori Festival, he's failed to present his Invitation Letter. Therefore, we can only suspect that he might've entered the country illegally.

response.speaker: Kujou Sara
response.text: And just a moment ago, we caught him in a Dandelion Wine crate near the Sailing Breeze.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Could we ask him a few questions?

response.speaker: Kujou Sara
response.text: If it would help shed any light on the situation, then please, be my guest.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, Venti... You didn't really come here illegally, did you?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Ouch, your words wound me... We've been apart for so long, and the moment we meet again, all I'm greeted with is grilling questions and suspicious glares.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: *sigh* You arrived in Inazuma via similar means, or, so I heard... You of all people should be more understanding, don't you think?

response.speaker: Kujou Sara
response.text: "Similar means"?

choices.text: Let's not bring up past now!

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Haha, I merely jest. Fear not, for the person who sent me the invitation is none other than Kamisato Ayato of Yashiro Commission. It's unlikely that someone acquainted with the likes of him would ever be here illegally, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But why weren't you on the same ship as the other bards?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Well, once I received the Invitation Letter, I couldn't help but want to come to Inazuma a little early. It was then that I happened upon a cargo ship bound for Inazuma transporting Dandelion Wine, so, naturally, I decided to set sail with them.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Once aboard, I found the captain to be a kindred spirit, and I was treated to an abundance of fine liquor along the way. Uh, I must have fallen asleep in the cargo crate while carefully comparing the tastes of Dandelion Wine and Inazuman sake.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: And when I woke up, I found myself in this warehouse with a Tenryou Commission general glaring at me from atop the crate.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Coming from Venti, this story is quite believable. But, it still feels a bit...

response.speaker: Hirayama
response.text: Excuse me, I'm the owner of the stolen goods from the Yae Publishing House, and there are some questions I would like to ask you.

response.speaker: Hirayama
response.text: Based on what you just said, it seems you've been in the warehouse for some time now. If that's the case, did you happen to hear anything unusual?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Actually, I did hear some faint footsteps around me a couple of times. But I didn't consider the sound anything out of the ordinary.

response.speaker: Hirayama
response.text: Hmm? But if you clearly heard something, why didn't you feel it was unusual?

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Oh, I seem to understand now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? What did you notice, Albedo?

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: When it comes to burglars, they are generally associated with prying or rummaging through things. What Venti means is that he did not hear anything unusual like that.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: As for the sound of footsteps, because this is a warehouse where many goods are coming in and out each day, it is quite normal for people to be walking around.

response.speaker: Hirayama
response.text: I see, but if that's the case, then we're back to square one regarding the stolen books.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: No, not quite. From the facts that have been presented to us, we can draw at least three conclusions now.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: First, whoever took the novels is not a spur-of-the-moment burglar, they had their sights on the books from the very beginning. Second, the culprit was very familiar with the warehouse and might even have a key. And third...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: There must be more than one criminal involved.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: #I knew you'd catch on, {NICKNAME}. One person couldn't possibly transport so many heavy books in such a short window of time, it must have been a team effort.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: It goes without saying that Venti clearly does not match up with our culprits.

response.speaker: Kujou Sara
response.text: Yes, I agree with your reasoning.

response.speaker: Kujou Sara
response.text: Mr. Hirayama, the Tenryou Commission will continue by investigating the warehouse staff. If you come across any further clues, please notify us immediately.

response.speaker: Hirayama
response.text: Yes, understood. I'll leave it to you, then.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Hee hee, I suppose I'm free as a bird then...

response.speaker: Kujou Sara
response.text: Not so fast. Even though we've cleared the theft allegations, we still haven't ascertained whether your arrival in Inazuma was legal or not.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Aw, 'tis a shame! I thought surely after my honest account you might let me off the hook.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sara's quite the meticulous one. So where's your Invitation Letter, Venti?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Yes, the Invitation Letter. Eh-he, I'm truly sorry. I can't seem to remember where I may have put it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh... How could you lose something so important!?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Don't be mistaken, I was well aware of how important it was. But I didn't bring any luggage with me, and the letter was too big to fit in my pocket, so I kept it in my hand the whole trip.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Strange... Though I had a little too much to drink, I know that I kept it in a secure place. I even recall being most pleased at coming up with a good idea at the time.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If you were holding the invitation in your hand the whole time, then why did you put it down?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Well, to properly compare the taste of Mondstadt wine and Inazuman sake, I had to hold a glass in each hand.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: I couldn't both hold the invitation and a glass at the same time. But surely I wouldn't put it in just any random place, it could easily be misplaced.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: #In which case, I believe there's only one place it could be. Have you figured it out, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? You're way ahead of Paimon! Do you two already know where the Invitation Letter is?

choices.text: You could say we're quite familiar...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: In his shoe?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, that doesn't sound right. The invitation is pretty big, isn't it? And, if it's in his shoe, he would feel it when he's walking!

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Haha, drinking too much may occasionally render the tongue a little numb, but it's true, it certainly wouldn't affect the feet.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: In his cape?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Are you sure? His cape doesn't even have any pockets to put stuff. But hey, a cape with pockets isn't a bad idea, you should try and get it tailored sometime, Venti.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Well, people do often claim that capes and the like serve no real purpose other than aesthetics, I suppose a cape with pockets would really turn the tables on that crowd.

dialogues.speaker: Murata
dialogues.text: Aratani and Kuroda are going back to Inazuma City to start printing extra copies of A Legend of Sword. I'll stay here and hold down the fort.

dialogues.speaker: Murata
dialogues.text: Of course, I still hope those novels can be found soon and that things won't take a turn for the worse.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Zhenyu... Hmm, sounds like a name from Liyue. Albedo, what kind of person is the author of this book?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I have not met him personally, but the editors said that he is actually the second son of the Feiyun Commerce Guild family in Liyue.

choices.text: The second son of the Feiyun Commerce Guild?

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Oh? Do you know him?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We've met on a couple of occasions.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, that's a real twist! Paimon never would have guessed that Xingqiu would be publishing a light novel together with Albedo!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But enough about that, Xingqiu would definitely be upset if he discovers that his books are missing.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's accompany Albedo to the warehouse, too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: According to the Arrival Schedule, there will be a ship arriving from Mondstadt today.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The artist for The Five Kasen portraits should be on board.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The boat should be arriving soon, so let's head down to the docks.
